title: DrivingSphere: Building a High-fidelity 4D World for Closed-loop Simulation

output_modality.value: 4D occupancy world (static OccDreamer scene plus dynamic actors), rendered to multi-view video by VideoDreamer.

control_signal.value: Regional BEV map plus text prompt for static occupancy; per-actor position, ID and caption, scene caption and camera intrinsics for video; driving agent control signals in the loop.

control_mechanism.value: OccDreamer: CLIP text by cross-attention, BEV map through a ControlNet branch. VideoDreamer: ST-DiT with ControlNet branch for occupancy features and cross-attention for actor and scene embeddings.

base_model.value: Occupancy VQVAE tokenizer plus diffusion denoiser; ST-DiT video denoiser with view-aware spatial attention; ControlNet inspired by PixArt-delta; T5 and CLIP text encoders.

datasets.value: nuScenes for video fidelity and agent tests; SemCity setup for occupancy generation. Figure 1 also mentions Waymo.

metrics.value: FVD, UniAD-based mAP, NDS, lane and drivable segmentation, L2; FID and MMD for occupancy; NC, DAC, TTC, PDMS open-loop; Route Completion and ADS closed-loop.

controllability_evidence.value: Generated video evaluated with UniAD: mAP 21.45 and NDS 34.16 versus 12.92 and 28.36 for MagicDrive; FVD 103.42. OccDreamer shows BEV map and text control qualitatively.

closed_loop.value: Yes; UniAD receives rendered video and outputs control on 100 pre-defined routes. Route Completion is 0.1170 (11.7% of each route on average), ADS 0.0851.

stated_limitations.value: Future work: improve dynamic agent behaviours and add more complex real-world scenarios.

notes: Trajectories of actors come from a transportation simulator per Figure 2 caption. Fidelity numbers are on generated data, not direct action-following errors.
